bias_targets.methodology: Annotated sentences from existing datasets using Best-Worst-Scaling (BWS) to generate continuous stereotype scores, trained Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) to predict these scores, and evaluated the ability of these scores to distinguish between sexist and non-sexist statements.

Generated continuous stereotype scores via crowdsourced BWS annotations, trained PLMs for score prediction, and evaluated predicted stereotype levels of race-targeted statements in multi-label hate speech datasets.

Annotated sentence pairs using BWS to quantify religious stereotypes on a continuous scale (-1 to 1), trained models to predict these scores, and evaluated correlations with downstream hate speech detection.
Extracted profession-related sentences from the StereoSet dataset, annotated them with continuous stereotype scores using BWS, and evaluated PLMs' predictive performance on these professional biases.

Used fine-tuned PLMs to predict continuous stereotype scores on disability-related sentences from the CrowS-Pairs dataset (comparing disadvantaged vs. advantaged groups) and the ETHOS hate speech dataset.
Applied stereotype-predicting PLMs to assess sentences regarding sexual orientation in the CrowS-Pairs dataset and multi-label hate speech datasets.
Evaluated PLM-predicted stereotype scores on sentences targeting national origin in hate speech data and nationality-based sentence pairs comparing advantaged and disadvantaged groups.
Tested fine-tuned PLMs on socioeconomic sentence pairs from the CrowS-Pairs dataset to compare predicted stereotype scores between disadvantaged and advantaged social classes.
Predicted continuous stereotype scores on age-related sentence pairs from the CrowS-Pairs dataset to evaluate score differences between disadvantaged and advantaged age groups.
Evaluated PLM-predicted continuous stereotype scores on physical appearance sentence pairs from the CrowS-Pairs dataset.
